course_name_original: Management and Economics of the Enterprise
course_name_en: Management and Economics of the Enterprise

learning_outcomes.text: Present the integration of production, operation, logistics and supply chain management in the era of the implementation of Industry 4.0 strategies and others that shape technical progress.
Apply generally valid economic theories and methods of management work.
Combine traditional procedures with rapidly developing information and communication means, hardware and software.
Handle decision-making methodology, quantitative and qualitative analysis and optimization.

syllabus_topics: Basics of financial management of the company for managers (the creation of the income statement, balance sheets and cash flow). Analysis of the tipping point, the relationship between business and innovation.
How to evaluate the level of business management. Analysis of absolute and ratio indicators from the income statement and balance sheets.
Marketing management and demand forecasting.
Aggregate and detailed production planning. From MRP to ERP.
Supply chain and logistics management, principles of modern production and operation management based on the pull principle.
Inventory management, economic model of order quantity (EOQ).
Stock management and statistically determined insurance stocks and time of order (ROP).
Inventory management according to fixed ordering intervals.
Technology development under the influence of Industry 4.0. Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), 5G networks, etc.
Total Quality Management. Basics of standardization, Kaizen philosophy, ISO standards.
Basics of project management, CMP and PERT methods, PMI, IPMA, Prince standards, limits.
Strategic management of a modern enterprise and development trends.
Sustainable production and the UN: "The 2030 agenda for Sustainable Development".
Business economics for managers, studying the growth of productivity and business efficiency, innovation and entrepreneurship.
Marketing management and demand forecasting. Including measurement of forecast accuracy.
Theory and models of decision-making under uncertainties and risks.
Japanese methods of production and operation management, types of equipment layout and workplace creation. Cellular manufacturing, grouping technology.
Capacity planning, computer-aided manufacturing. Designing production systems, technological design and standardization.
Labor economics, principles of specialization, job rotation, work standardization and motivation.
Logistics and inventory management. EOQ, ROP, FOI models.
Management of MRP material requirements, master production plan (Master Schedule, Bill of Materials, Inventory records file), production batch size.
Aggregate planning, Master Production Schedule (MPS). Just-in-Time Excellence. Kanban System, transition to JiT. Scheduling.
Total Quality Management. Quality characteristics, TQM, Kaizen philosophy. ISO.
Maintenance management systems, preventive and predictive maintenance.
Project management, PERT and CMP, advantages and limitations.
Strategic management of a modern enterprise, presentation of case studies throughout the course.
assessment_rules: To be granted credit, students need attendance, active participation, and a seminar paper. The final exam consists of two parts: a written test and an oral part. The written test has 3 simple examples (max 5 points each) and 5 definitional questions (max 2 points each). A minimum of 15 points in the written test is required to proceed to the oral part of the exam.
